requirements: Reproduce DSpark, a speculative decoding framework combining semi-autoregressive draft generation with confidence-scheduled verification, matching the paper's offline benchmark results and characterizing its production deployment behavior.

sub_tasks.requirements: Set up the training and inference environment, target models, tokenizers, and dependencies required for training DSpark drafters and running speculative decoding experiments across offline benchmarks and (where applicable) production deployment.
Provision the software environment and repository scaffolding needed to train and evaluate DSpark, DFlash, and Eagle3 drafters.

Code has been implemented to install a working Python environment with PyTorch and CUDA support compatible with running large-scale LLM inference and drafter training (e.g., a requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, or environment setup script that pins compatible versions of torch, transformers, and CUDA toolkit).

verification.spec: Check that repository root contains a dependency manifest (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, or setup.py/environment.yml) that pins torch, transformers, and CUDA-compatible versions. Programmatically parse the file and assert 'torch' and 'transformers' appear with version specifiers, then run `python -c 'import torch; assert torch.cuda.is_available()'` in the created environment.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that provides a training entry point (script or CLI) exposing configurable flags for target model, drafter type (Eagle3 / DFlash / DSpark), number of drafter layers, block size gamma, sequential head type (markov/rnn), and Open-PerfectBlend data path.

verification.spec: Run the training entry point with `--help` and confirm the CLI exposes flags for: target model id/path, drafter type (choices include eagle3, dflash, dspark), number of drafter layers, block size gamma, sequential head type (choices markov, rnn), and Open-PerfectBlend data path. Additionally run a dry-run invocation (e.g., 1 optimizer step on tiny data) using --drafter-type dspark --sequential-head markov --gamma 7 --num-layers 2 and confirm it initializes and steps without error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that provides an inference/evaluation entry point runnable in speculative decoding mode with a specified target model and drafter checkpoint, temperature=1.0, and chain-based drafting, matching the offline evaluation protocol described in Section 4.1.

verification.spec: Invoke the evaluation entry point with a small target model (e.g., Qwen3-4B) and a trained DSpark drafter checkpoint on a 10-example subset of GSM8K, passing --temperature 1.0 and --draft-mode chain. Verify that: (1) the run completes without error, (2) logs indicate speculative decoding was active (draft proposals + target verification), (3) sampling temperature used equals 1.0, (4) drafting is chain-based (no tree expansion), and (5) an accepted-length metric tau is printed per example.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that organizes the DeepSpec-style repository so Eagle3, DFlash, and DSpark drafters share a common training/eval framework (identical training data pipeline, target-feature-layer selection, block-size configuration) enabling the strict apples-to-apples retraining protocol in Section 4.1.

verification.spec: Inspect the repository layout and confirm Eagle3, DFlash, and DSpark are registered under a shared drafter interface (e.g., a common base class or registry). Verify all three drafters are trained via the same top-level training script/config schema, use the same data-loading pipeline for Open-PerfectBlend, and accept the same --target-feature-layers argument. Launch tiny training runs for each of the three drafter types using identical configs (target, data, feature layers, block size) and confirm identical batch iterators are used.

sub_tasks.requirements: Acquire and configure the target models and tokenizers used in the offline experiments.

Code has been implemented to download and load the Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Qwen3-14B target model weights and their tokenizers from a public checkpoint source (e.g., Hugging Face), and to instantiate them in non-thinking mode as specified in Section 4.1.

verification.spec: Run a script that invokes the repository's model-loading utility for each of Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B; assert AutoModelForCausalLM and AutoTokenizer load successfully from HuggingFace ids (Qwen/Qwen3-4B, Qwen/Qwen3-8B, Qwen/Qwen3-14B), and that generation is invoked in non-thinking mode (e.g., enable_thinking=False or equivalent config flag).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to download and load the Gemma4-12B target model weights and tokenizer used as the cross-family target in Table 1.

verification.spec: Run a script that loads Gemma4-12B (google/gemma-4-12b or the referenced Gemma4 checkpoint id) via AutoModelForCausalLM and AutoTokenizer; assert the model instantiates on GPU and can produce a single-token forward pass output tensor.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to freeze all parameters of the target model during drafter training, and to share (and freeze) the target model's token embedding layer and language modeling head with the drafter, as specified in Sections 2.2 and 3.3.

verification.spec: Instantiate the joint (target + drafter) training module. Assert that (1) all parameters of the target model have requires_grad=False; (2) the drafter's token embedding module and lm_head module are the same Python objects (or share the same weight tensors via reference) as the target model's embed_tokens and lm_head; (3) those shared modules also have requires_grad=False; (4) after one optimizer step on dummy data, target parameters and shared embedding/lm_head weights are unchanged (bitwise) while the drafter's backbone/sequential/confidence parameters have changed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to expose hidden states from a configurable set of target-model feature layers {l_1, ..., l_m} for KV/context injection into the drafter, using the same feature layers for Eagle3, DFlash, and DSpark to satisfy the fair-comparison requirement of Section 4.1.

verification.spec: Instantiate the target-feature-extraction wrapper with a configurable feature_layers list (e.g., [2, 15, 27]). Run a forward pass and verify the returned context feature has shape (batch, seq, m*d) where m=len(feature_layers), matching the concatenation described in Eq. for c. Then instantiate Eagle3, DFlash, and DSpark drafters with the same feature_layers argument and verify each accepts and consumes the same-shaped context tensor.

sub_tasks.requirements: Configure distributed training infrastructure (HAI-LLM-style) with the system-level optimizations needed to train drafters on top of frozen large target models.

Code has been implemented to support distributed (multi-GPU) training of the drafter with the target model kept frozen, including a data-parallel or model-parallel strategy compatible with target models up to at least ~14B parameters.

verification.spec: Launch the training script with --target Qwen3-14B --drafter dspark on 8 H100 GPUs using the configured distributed strategy (e.g., FSDP or tensor-parallel). Verify (1) training initializes without OOM, (2) the target model is sharded/distributed such that no single GPU holds the full 14B weights in trainable state, (3) at least 5 optimizer steps complete, (4) drafter gradients synchronize across workers (verify by checking that after a step, drafter weights are identical on all ranks via torch.distributed.all_reduce equality check).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the hidden-state communication optimization: the target model's pre-LM-head hidden states (dimension d) are cached and communicated across workers instead of full-vocabulary logits, and the frozen LM head is applied locally on the drafter workers only at sampled target positions, as described in Section 5.1.

verification.spec: Instrument the training pipeline's inter-worker communication layer: mock or hook the send/recv calls and assert that the tensor payload shape sent from target-model workers has last-dim == hidden_size d (not vocab_size V). Additionally verify that a local LM-head projection is invoked on drafter workers only for sampled anchor positions (not the full sequence).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for anchor-bounded sequence packing: a fixed number of draft anchors is sampled per training sequence, isolated gamma-token prediction blocks are packed into dense batches, and causal masking across independent packed sequences/anchors is enforced via token-level attention indices (not standard 2D padding masks), as described in Section 5.1.

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic batch of multiple training sequences with multiple sampled anchors per sequence, pass it through the packing utility, and assert (1) the number of anchor blocks per sequence equals the configured fixed count, (2) the returned tensors are densely packed without padding tokens, and (3) the token-level attention indices produce a causal mask that isolates each anchor block (i.e., token positions in different blocks have zero attention weight to each other).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to randomly sample multiple anchor positions per training sequence and form gamma-token blocks from each anchor as the unit of drafter supervision, matching the training data construction described in Section 3.3.

verification.spec: Instantiate the drafter training dataset with a fixed sequence and num_anchors_per_seq=K (e.g., K=8), gamma=7. Iterate the dataset multiple times and verify: (1) each training example is a gamma-token block anchored at some position within the source sequence; (2) across epochs, the sampled anchor positions vary randomly (not deterministic); (3) blocks respect sequence boundaries (anchor + gamma <= seq_len); (4) approximately K anchors per source sequence are yielded per epoch.

sub_tasks.requirements: Configure drafter hyperparameters and training-loop settings that establish the experimental setup (block size, drafter depth, training epochs, sampling parameters).

Code has been implemented so that, by default, DSpark and DFlash drafters use 5 transformer layers and Eagle3 uses 1 layer, with the same block size gamma=7 used for training and offline evaluation (Section 4.1). Depth and block size must be configurable to support the ablations in Figures 3 and 4.

verification.spec: Load default config files for DSpark, DFlash, and Eagle3 drafters. Assert num_layers == 5 for DSpark and DFlash, num_layers == 1 for Eagle3, and block_size (gamma) == 7 for all three. Also assert num_layers and block_size are exposed as configurable CLI/config arguments (not hardcoded).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that Eagle3's Training-Time Test (TTT) horizon is aligned to 7 (matching the block size used by DFlash and DSpark) for the strict fair-comparison retraining described in Section 4.1.

verification.spec: Load the Eagle3 drafter training config and assert the TTT horizon parameter (e.g., ttt_horizon or draft_length) equals 7, matching the gamma used by DFlash/DSpark.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each drafter is trained for 10 epochs on the Open-PerfectBlend training data (as specified in Section 4.1), with a training loop that iterates over the packed anchor-block batches until 10 full passes are completed.

verification.spec: Inspect the drafter training config/script: assert num_epochs == 10 (or equivalent max-steps computed as 10 * len(dataset) / batch_size). Optionally run a smoke training loop and confirm epoch counter reaches 10 before termination.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that speculative decoding evaluation uses sampling temperature 1.0 with standard (chain-based) rejection-sampling speculative decoding, and reports accepted length tau per decoding round including the target-generated bonus token, matching the evaluation protocol footnotes of Section 4.1.

verification.spec: Invoke the offline evaluation entrypoint with default arguments. Assert sampling temperature == 1.0, verification uses standard chain-based speculative decoding with rejection sampling, and the reported accepted-length tau counts the bonus token (i.e., for a fully-rejected block tau == 1, not 0). Verify by running a single prompt where the drafter proposes tokens intentionally mismatched to the target and confirm tau == 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Prepare the Open-PerfectBlend prompts and regenerate responses with each target model under the specified non-thinking mode and sampling parameters to build drafter training data.
Acquire and stage the Open-PerfectBlend source dataset used for DSpark drafter training.
Code has been implemented to download the Open-PerfectBlend instruction dataset (the open-sourced version of PerfectBlend) from its public source and store it locally for downstream processing.

verification.spec: Run the dataset download script (e.g., `python scripts/download_open_perfectblend.py --output-dir data/opb`). Verify (1) the script exits with return code 0, (2) the resulting directory contains the Open-PerfectBlend files, and (3) the loaded dataset (via HuggingFace datasets or equivalent) reports a non-empty split.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that loads the acquired Open-PerfectBlend dataset and verifies it contains approximately 1.3 million samples, aborting with a clear error if the count is materially different.

verification.spec: Invoke the dataset loader function on the downloaded Open-PerfectBlend directory. Assert that len(dataset) is within [1.2M, 1.4M] samples (matching the stated ~1.3M). Then artificially truncate the dataset to 100 samples and assert the loader raises a clear error message referencing an expected count.

sub_tasks.requirements: The loaded Open-PerfectBlend dataset exposes per-sample domain labels or metadata sufficient to identify chat, math, code, and instruction-following subsets so that the domain mixture can be inspected.

verification.spec: Load the Open-PerfectBlend dataset via the provided loader. Assert each sample has a field (e.g., 'domain' or 'source' or equivalent metadata) that can be mapped to one of {chat, math, code, instruction-following}. Compute the empirical domain distribution and assert all four categories are present with non-zero counts, and that the proportions roughly match the paper (chat ~17.6%, math ~39.4%, code ~38.9%, IF ~4.1%) within +-5 absolute percentage points.

sub_tasks.requirements: The prepared Open-PerfectBlend domain mixture matches the reported composition: approximately 17.6% chat, 39.4% math, 38.9% code, and 4.1% instruction-following.

verification.spec: After preparing the training data, iterate over all samples and classify each by domain tag (chat/math/code/instruction-following). Compute the fraction of each and assert chat ≈ 17.6%, math ≈ 39.4%, code ≈ 38.9%, instruction ≈ 4.1% within tolerance. Report the chat percentage as the measured value.

sub_tasks.requirements: Extract prompts only from Open-PerfectBlend and discard the original responses so that responses can be regenerated by each target model.
Code has been implemented that extracts the prompt/instruction field from every Open-PerfectBlend sample and writes prompts-only records to disk, explicitly dropping any pre-existing response field.

verification.spec: Run the prompt-extraction script on the loaded Open-PerfectBlend dataset. Verify the output file (jsonl or parquet) contains one record per source sample with a 'prompt' field and no 'response'/'answer'/'output' field. Inspect random samples and confirm the prompt text matches the original instruction. Additionally construct a synthetic sample with a pre-existing response field and confirm the extraction drops it.

sub_tasks.requirements: The prompts-only artifact preserves a stable ordering or unique identifier per prompt so that regenerated responses can be joined back to their originating prompt without ambiguity.

verification.spec: Inspect the prompts-only artifact and verify each record has a unique identifier field (e.g., 'prompt_id' or 'idx') OR the records are stored in a stable, index-addressable order (e.g., a parquet file whose row index is used). Assert that ids are unique across the dataset (no collisions) and that a downstream join-utility function exists that maps generated responses back to their prompt by this identifier.

sub_tasks.requirements: Regenerate responses for the Open-PerfectBlend prompts using each target model in non-thinking mode with the model's recommended sampling parameters.

Code has been implemented to run batched response generation over the extracted Open-PerfectBlend prompts for each target model in the study (Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, and Gemma4-12B), producing one response file per target model.

verification.spec: Invoke the batched response-generation script on a small subset (e.g., 100 prompts) of the extracted prompts, once per target model in {Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, Gemma4-12B}. For each target verify: (1) the script produces exactly one response file named after / annotated with the target model, (2) each output record has fields (prompt_id, response, target_model), (3) the number of responses equals the number of input prompts.

sub_tasks.requirements: The generation code applies each target model's chat template and generation-time flags such that responses are produced in non-thinking mode (e.g., disabling any reasoning/thinking segments for Qwen3 models).

verification.spec: Inspect the generation code and confirm: (1) for Qwen3 models the chat template is applied with enable_thinking=False (or equivalent flag) so no <think>...</think> segments are emitted; (2) for Gemma4 the appropriate non-thinking chat template is used. Then generate responses for 20 sample prompts using Qwen3-4B and grep the outputs for '<think>' tokens or reasoning trace markers; assert none are present.

sub_tasks.requirements: The generation code uses each target model's officially recommended sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, top-k, repetition penalty as applicable) rather than arbitrary defaults, and these parameters are recorded alongside the outputs.

verification.spec: Inspect the generation configuration files/code and verify each target model has an explicit dict of sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, top_k, repetition_penalty as applicable) that matches the model card's officially recommended values (e.g., for Qwen3 non-thinking: temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, min_p=0). Assert that these parameters are also serialized into a metadata file (e.g., generation_config.json) written alongside the response outputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The response-generation pipeline supports resumable execution and deduplication so that partially generated shards can be continued without producing duplicate (prompt, target_model) responses.

verification.spec: Start the generation pipeline on 50 prompts, kill it after ~25 have been generated (SIGINT), then re-invoke the same command. Verify: (1) re-invocation resumes and only processes the remaining ~25 prompts (fewer target-model forward passes than a from-scratch run), (2) the final output file contains exactly 50 unique (prompt_id, target_model) records with no duplicates, (3) if a duplicate (prompt_id, target_model) already exists it is skipped rather than regenerated.

sub_tasks.requirements: Package the regenerated (prompt, response) pairs into the final drafter training corpus used by DSpark, Eagle3, and DFlash.

Code has been implemented that assembles per-target-model training corpora by concatenating each prompt with its regenerated response using the target model's tokenizer and chat template, yielding tokenized sequences suitable for drafter training.

verification.spec: Run the corpus-assembly script for target=Qwen3-4B on 100 (prompt, response) pairs. Verify each output record is a tokenized sequence produced by (a) applying Qwen3-4B's chat template to concatenate prompt+response with the correct role tags, (b) tokenizing with Qwen3-4B's tokenizer. Detokenize a sample and confirm the reconstructed text contains both the original prompt and response and matches Qwen3-4B's chat-template formatting exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: The training corpus construction records, for every sample, which target model produced the response, so that the same corpus is used consistently across DSpark, Eagle3, and DFlash training for a given target.

verification.spec: Inspect the assembled training corpus files and verify each record (or the parent directory/metadata) records a 'target_model' field identifying which target produced the response. Then run the DSpark, Eagle3, and DFlash training entry points for target=Qwen3-4B with default corpus paths and confirm all three drafters load from the same Qwen3-4B-tagged corpus file (checked via logged data path or a hash of the input records).

sub_tasks.requirements: The final per-target training corpus retains coverage across all four Open-PerfectBlend domains (chat, math, code, instruction-following) with proportions consistent with the source mixture, verified by a domain-count summary emitted during preparation.

verification.spec: Run the corpus preparation pipeline end-to-end for one target model, and inspect the summary log/JSON it emits. Assert the summary reports counts for all four domains {chat, math, code, instruction-following}, all counts are > 0, and the proportions are within +-5 absolute percentage points of the source Open-PerfectBlend mixture (17.6/39.4/38.9/4.1).

sub_tasks.requirements: Prepare all offline evaluation benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME25, MBPP, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench, MT-Bench, Alpaca, Arena-Hard) with correct splits, prompts, and sampling protocol (temperature 1.0, chain-based drafting).
Acquire and prepare the mathematical reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME25) with correct splits and prompt formatting.
Code has been implemented to download/load the GSM8K test set (the standard test split used for evaluation of mathematical reasoning) and expose its problems as prompts.

verification.spec: Invoke the GSM8K loader (e.g., datasets.load_dataset('gsm8k', 'main', split='test')) via the repository's benchmark utility. Assert: (1) the returned object has ~1319 examples (the standard GSM8K test split size), (2) each example has a 'question' field exposed as a prompt string, (3) a helper function like get_prompts('gsm8k') returns a list of these question strings.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the MATH500 subset (the 500-problem evaluation split introduced by Lightman et al.) with correct problem identifiers.

verification.spec: Invoke the dataset loader for MATH500; assert that exactly 500 problems are returned, each with a problem statement and reference answer, and that a small sample of problem IDs matches those defined by Lightman et al.'s MATH500 split.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load AIME25 problems as the evaluation set for competition-level math reasoning.

verification.spec: Invoke the AIME25 loader; verify that it returns the 30 AIME 2025 problems (Zhang and Math-AI, 2025) with problem text and numeric answers accessible.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to format each math benchmark prompt using each target model's recommended chat template in non-thinking mode, consistent with the training-data generation protocol.

verification.spec: For each supported target model (Qwen3-*, Gemma4-12B), pass a sample math prompt through the formatter; assert that the output string starts with the model's expected chat-template BOS/role markers and does NOT contain any thinking-mode markers (e.g., no <think> tags for Qwen3 non-thinking mode).

sub_tasks.requirements: Acquire and prepare the code generation benchmarks (MBPP, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench) with correct splits and prompts.
Code has been implemented to load the MBPP evaluation split with proper problem prompts for code generation.

verification.spec: Invoke the MBPP loader; assert it returns the MBPP evaluation split with problem prompts, test lists, and reference solutions accessible per problem.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the HumanEval problem set (164 problems) with function signatures and docstrings as prompts.

verification.spec: Invoke the HumanEval loader; assert that exactly 164 problems are returned, each providing a function signature and docstring usable as a prompt.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load LiveCodeBench problems (Jain et al., 2025) with the evaluation prompt format used in the paper's LCB column.

verification.spec: Invoke the LiveCodeBench loader; assert it returns problems in the LCB evaluation format (with problem statement and test cases), and that at least one sample prompt matches the LiveCodeBench schema (Jain et al., 2025).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to render each code-benchmark prompt through the target model's chat template in non-thinking mode, matching the setup used for speculative decoding rollouts.

verification.spec: For each target model, pass a sample code-benchmark prompt through the formatter; assert the output uses the model's chat template in non-thinking mode (contains expected role markers, no thinking tags).

sub_tasks.requirements: Acquire and prepare the daily-chat benchmarks (MT-Bench, Alpaca, Arena-Hard) with correct prompts.
Code has been implemented to load MT-Bench prompts (multi-turn evaluation questions from Zheng et al., 2023) as chat evaluation inputs.

verification.spec: Invoke the MT-Bench loader; assert it returns the 80 MT-Bench questions across the expected categories with multi-turn structure (Zheng et al., 2023).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the Alpaca evaluation prompts (from Taori et al., 2023) for the daily-chat evaluation column.

verification.spec: Invoke the Alpaca evaluation loader; assert it returns AlpacaEval prompts (Taori et al., 2023) with each item exposing an 'instruction' field usable as a prompt.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load Arena-Hard prompts (Li et al., 2024a; 2025b) as the third daily-chat benchmark.

verification.spec: Invoke the Arena-Hard loader; assert it returns Arena-Hard prompts (v1/v2 per Li et al., 2024a; 2025b) with each item providing a user question.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to apply each target model's non-thinking-mode chat template to MT-Bench, Alpaca, and Arena-Hard prompts prior to speculative decoding.

verification.spec: For each of MT-Bench, Alpaca, and Arena-Hard, format a sample prompt through the target model's chat template in non-thinking mode; assert the rendered string uses the correct role markers and omits thinking tags.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the evaluation-time sampling and decoding protocol used across all nine benchmarks.
Code has been implemented to run standard (lossless) speculative decoding with sampling temperature fixed to 1.0 for all offline benchmark evaluations.

verification.spec: Run a short speculative decoding rollout on a toy prompt with sampling temperature=1.0; assert that (a) the acceptance rule implemented follows the standard Chen et al. 2023 / Leviathan et al. 2023 rejection sampling with min(1, p_t/p_d), (b) temperature is applied consistently to both draft and target distributions, and (c) the config exposes temperature=1.0 as the default for benchmark eval.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that all drafters (Eagle3, DFlash, DSpark) use chain-based drafting (not tree-based) during offline benchmark evaluation.

verification.spec: Instantiate each drafter (Eagle3, DFlash, DSpark) with the eval config; assert the drafting mode is 'chain' and that tree-based drafting/tree-attention codepaths are disabled (each decoding round produces a single linear chain of γ candidate tokens).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to disable the confidence scheduler during offline benchmark evaluation, so drafters propose a fixed block of tokens (per Section 4.2).

verification.spec: Run DSpark in offline-benchmark evaluation mode on a short prompt; assert that the confidence scheduler is disabled (verification length equals the configured fixed γ for every step) and that the number of tokens sent to the target verifier per step is constant.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute the accepted length tau per decoding round including the target-generated bonus token, matching the metric definition in Section 4.1 footnote 4.

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic rollout with a known sequence of accepted/rejected draft tokens (e.g., 3 accepted drafts + 1 rejected + 1 bonus token from target). Assert that the accepted-length computation returns 4 (3 accepted drafts + 1 bonus), matching the footnote 4 definition.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to aggregate per-request accepted-length measurements into an average tau per benchmark and to organize the nine benchmarks into the three domains (Math, Code, Chat) used in Table 1.

verification.spec: Feed a small set of per-request accepted-length lists into the aggregator; assert it (a) computes the arithmetic mean τ per benchmark and (b) groups {GSM8K, MATH500, AIME25} under 'Math', {MBPP, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench} under 'Code', and {MT-Bench, Alpaca, Arena-Hard} under 'Chat', matching Table 1's column structure.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the DFlash-based semi-autoregressive parallel backbone that produces per-position hidden states h_k and base logits U_k for a block of γ positions via a single forward pass, using KV injection from target hidden states, a mask-token block input with anchor-as-first-position, bidirectional block attention, and a shared frozen embedding/LM head.
Code implements the KV injection pathway that extracts hidden states from a configured set of target-model layers {l_1,...,l_m} and injects them into every draft-backbone layer.

Code has been implemented to expose forward-pass hooks (or an equivalent mechanism) on the target model that capture the hidden-state activations from a configurable set of target layer indices {l_1,...,l_m} during prefill.

verification.spec: Instantiate the target model with a configurable list of hook layer indices {l_1,...,l_m}; run a forward pass and assert that hidden-state tensors are captured for exactly those layer indices with the expected shape (batch, seq, d) each. Confirm the layer index list is user-configurable.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to concatenate the captured target hidden states from the m selected layers along the hidden dimension for each token position, producing a feature tensor of size m*d per position.

verification.spec: Given m captured hidden-state tensors of shape (B, T, d), invoke the concatenation utility and assert the output has shape (B, T, m*d) and that slicing the last dim into m chunks of size d recovers the original per-layer tensors in order.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a shared linear projection W_c ∈ R^{d x m*d} that maps the concatenated target-layer features into the draft hidden dimension d, producing per-position context features c_i.

verification.spec: Instantiate the context projection module; assert it contains a linear layer with weight shape (d, m*d) that is shared (single instance) across positions, and that applying it to an input of shape (B, T, m*d) yields an output of shape (B, T, d).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that in every draft-backbone attention layer, the injected context features c_i are concatenated with the current draft block's key/value tensors along the sequence dimension, so that draft queries attend jointly to the block and to the injected target context.

verification.spec: Hook the attention module in a draft-backbone transformer layer. Feed a small batch and assert that within each layer's attention call, the key and value tensors have sequence length == block_size + context_feature_length (i.e., the injected context features c_i are concatenated to K/V along the sequence dim). Verify this happens in every draft layer, not just the first.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the context features c_i are computed once per prefill and cached, and are reused across draft-model forward passes without recomputation during a single decoding round.

verification.spec: Run one prefill + multiple draft-forward passes for the same request; instrument the context-projection module to count invocations. Assert that the projection is called exactly once per prefill and 0 additional times across subsequent draft forward passes (features are cached and reused within the decoding round).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that when target-model hidden states change, the injected keys/values propagated into the draft backbone change accordingly, and that disabling injection changes the draft logits, confirming that the KV-injection pathway is functionally active.

verification.spec: Unit test: (1) perturb the target hidden states passed into the KV-injection pathway and assert the resulting keys/values entering the draft backbone differ from the unperturbed run; (2) disable KV injection (e.g., zero out injected context or bypass concat) and assert draft logits differ from the injection-enabled run on the same inputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the block input construction where the anchor token serves as the first prediction position followed by γ-1 mask token embeddings, so that γ input positions yield γ draft logits.

Code has been implemented that defines a dedicated MASK token embedding (either a reserved vocabulary id or a learned/frozen extra embedding vector) used to fill the γ-1 non-anchor input positions of the draft block.

verification.spec: Instantiate the draft model; assert a MASK token embedding exists (either a reserved vocabulary id with a corresponding embedding row, or a dedicated learned/frozen vector). Verify that when building the γ-length draft input, positions 2..γ all use this exact MASK embedding vector.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that constructs the draft-block input as [embed(anchor_token), MASK, MASK, ..., MASK] with total length γ, placing the anchor (the target's last generated bonus token) at position 1.

verification.spec: Call the draft-input construction function with a specific anchor_token_id and block size gamma. Assert the returned input embedding tensor has shape (batch, gamma, hidden), that position 0 equals embed(anchor_token_id), and positions 1..gamma-1 equal the MASK token embedding.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the backbone emits γ output logits, one per input position, where position 1 predicts the token following the anchor (i.e., the anchor itself is treated as a prediction position), deviating from the original DFlash convention of anchor + γ mask -> γ predictions.

verification.spec: Run the backbone forward with block size gamma=7 and assert the output logits tensor has shape (batch, 7, vocab_size). Feed anchor_token='A' followed by 6 masks and confirm the logits at position 0 correspond to predicting the token following the anchor (differing from a pure-mask baseline that would predict the anchor itself).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that changing the anchor token changes the logits at position 1 (and downstream positions), while changing a masked position leaves logits unchanged (since it is a fixed MASK embedding), confirming the anchor-as-first-position input semantics.

verification.spec: Unit test: (a) run the draft backbone with two different anchor tokens and identical mask positions; assert logits at position 1 (and ≥ one downstream position) differ. (b) run with the same anchor but replace the input embedding at a masked position with an arbitrary other vector while keeping the semantic 'mask' role; assert that the model's MASK-based construction ignores per-position input variation (i.e., the code always fills those positions with the fixed MASK embedding, so logits are unchanged).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the block size γ is a configurable hyperparameter (supporting at least γ ∈ {4,5,7,8,12,15,16}) and the input construction and output logits shape adjust accordingly.

verification.spec: For each γ in {4,5,7,8,12,15,16}, instantiate the draft model with block_size=γ and run one forward pass. Assert that (a) the input tensor has length γ (1 anchor + γ-1 masks) and (b) the output logits tensor has shape (B, γ, V).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements bidirectional (non-causal) self-attention across the γ block positions, while still respecting causal ordering with respect to prompt context and the injected KV features.

Code has been implemented that constructs the attention mask so that every position within the γ-length draft block attends bidirectionally to every other position within the same block (fully connected block-internal attention).

verification.spec: Extract the attention mask used inside the draft block during forward pass. Assert that the submatrix corresponding to the gamma block positions is all-ones (or equivalent additive 0), i.e., there is no causal triangular masking within the block.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that draft-block positions can also attend to the injected target context features (from the KV-injection pathway) alongside the block itself.

verification.spec: Inspect the attention mask/index structure used inside each draft layer; assert that each of the γ draft positions can attend to (i) all other γ positions in the block (bidirectionally) AND (ii) the injected target context feature positions concatenated along the sequence dim of keys/values. Perturbing a context-feature vector should change the draft attention output.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that permuting the non-anchor block positions in the attention connectivity does not break shape/mask correctness, and that a purely causal mask produces different logits from the bidirectional block mask, confirming that bidirectional attention is actually applied.

verification.spec: Build the backbone attention module and run two forward passes on identical input: (1) with the bidirectional block mask, (2) with a purely causal mask. Assert output logits differ by max-abs > 1e-4. Then permute non-anchor block positions in input+mask consistently and verify output shape unchanged and no NaN/inf.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports optional sliding-window attention (window size 128 for the production deployment configuration) over the prompt/context sequence while retaining bidirectional attention within the draft block.

verification.spec: Construct the backbone with sliding_window=128 enabled. Inspect the attention mask/bias tensor used for the prompt context and verify that positions farther than 128 tokens apart are masked (masked value is -inf or attention weight is 0), while draft-block positions attend bidirectionally to each other (no causal mask within the gamma-token block). Also verify the sliding-window size is a configurable parameter.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the draft backbone as a stack of transformer layers producing per-position hidden states h_k, with configurable depth and shared frozen embedding/LM head.
Code has been implemented for a configurable stack of N transformer decoder layers forming the draft backbone, supporting depths N ∈ {1, 2, 5} as used in the depth ablation.

verification.spec: Instantiate the draft backbone with num_layers=1, 2, and 5 via the config API. For each, assert len(backbone.layers)==N and that each layer is a transformer decoder layer (has self-attention and MLP submodules).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each transformer layer in the backbone applies the KV-injection augmentation and the bidirectional block-attention mask specified above, in that order.

verification.spec: Inspect the forward method of a single backbone layer (or trace via hooks) and confirm it (a) concatenates target-model context features into K/V (KV-injection) and (b) applies the bidirectional block attention mask. Ablating KV-injection (zeroing context) must change layer output; ablating bidirectionality (using causal mask) must also change layer output.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports a MoE-based backbone variant (three MoE layers with mHC and sliding window attention of 128) used for the DeepSeek-V4 production deployment configuration.

verification.spec: Load the DSpark-V4 production backbone config and assert: exactly 3 layers, each layer is MoE (has expert routing module), mHC is enabled in attention config, and sliding_window==128.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the backbone forward returns a tensor of per-position hidden states h_1,...,h_γ of shape (γ, d), which are exposed for downstream consumption by the sequential head and confidence head.

verification.spec: Call backbone.forward on a batch of shape (B, gamma) and assert the returned hidden states tensor has shape (B, gamma, d) where d==hidden_size. Confirm the tensor is exposed as a named attribute or return value accessible to sequential and confidence heads.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that a forward pass through the backbone on a batch of dummy inputs produces hidden-state tensors with the expected shape (batch, γ, d) and finite (non-NaN, non-Inf) values.

verification.spec: Construct the DSpark parallel backbone with a small config (e.g., d=128, 2 layers, gamma=7). Feed a random dummy batch of shape (batch=4, gamma=7) of token ids plus mock target hidden states. Assert the returned hidden states tensor has shape (4, 7, 128), dtype is a floating point type, and torch.isfinite(h).all() is True.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the shared frozen embedding layer and LM head coming from the target model, and computes base logits U_k = LMHead(h_k) for each block position.
Code has been implemented that loads the target model's token embedding matrix and language-modeling-head weights into the draft model and marks their parameters with requires_grad=False (frozen).

verification.spec: After constructing the draft model from a target model, assert draft.embed_tokens.weight.data_ptr() equals target.embed_tokens.weight.data_ptr() (or their values are exactly equal) and similarly for the LM head. Also assert draft.embed_tokens.weight.requires_grad == False and draft.lm_head.weight.requires_grad == False.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the draft backbone uses the frozen shared embedding to embed both the anchor token and any previously-sampled token IDs consumed by the sequential head.

verification.spec: Verify that the backbone's token embedding layer is set to the target model's embedding (same tensor id or shared weight). Assert requires_grad==False. Run forward with anchor token ID and confirm the embedded vector equals target_model.embed_tokens(anchor_id).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes base logits U_k ∈ R^{|V|} for each block position k by applying the shared frozen LM head to h_k, yielding a tensor of shape (batch, γ, |V|).

verification.spec: Run backbone forward and confirm the returned base-logits tensor U has shape (batch, gamma, vocab_size). Assert U == frozen_lm_head(h) by recomputing lm_head(h) manually and comparing tensors elementwise with torch.allclose.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that after a training/optimization step, the embedding and LM-head parameter tensors are byte-for-byte unchanged (frozen), while backbone parameters have changed.

verification.spec: Snapshot state_dict of embedding and LM head before one optimizer.step() on a synthetic batch. After the step, assert torch.equal for every embedding and LM-head tensor (byte-identical). Assert at least one backbone parameter tensor has changed (not equal to its snapshot).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that base logits U_k produced by LMHead(h_k) have shape (batch, γ, |V|) matching the target model's vocabulary size, and that argmax over U_1 with a controlled input matches the LM-head's output when applied to h_1 independently.

verification.spec: Forward a batch through backbone+LMHead, obtain U of shape (B, gamma, |V|). Assert |V|==target.config.vocab_size. Then compute LMHead(h_1) independently and verify U[:,0,:] matches within 1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements an end-to-end backbone forward interface that ties together KV injection, block-input construction, bidirectional attention, and the shared LM head, and behaves correctly on integration tests.

Code has been implemented that exposes a single forward function draft_backbone(anchor_token, target_hidden_states, block_size γ) returning both the per-position hidden states {h_k} and base logits {U_k} in a single pass.

verification.spec: Call draft_backbone(anchor_token, target_hidden_states, gamma) and assert it returns a tuple/dict with keys 'hidden_states' of shape (batch, gamma, d) and 'logits' of shape (batch, gamma, V), in a single invocation (no internal loop over gamma).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the backbone forward function performs exactly one transformer forward pass regardless of block size γ (verified by counting attention-layer invocations or by wall-clock scaling being sub-linear in γ).

verification.spec: Monkey-patch the transformer layer's forward to increment a global counter. Call draft_backbone with gamma in {4,8,12,16}; assert the counter increments by exactly num_layers each time (independent of gamma). Alternatively, measure wall-clock and assert time(gamma=16) / time(gamma=4) < 2.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: An integration test verifies that calling the backbone forward twice with identical inputs yields bit-identical outputs (deterministic behavior in eval mode).

verification.spec: Set backbone.eval(), seed torch/CUDA, run backbone.forward twice on the same input tensor, and assert torch.equal on the outputs (bit-identical).

sub_tasks.requirements: An integration test verifies that when the sequential head and confidence head are disabled (identity/zero contribution), the argmax of the backbone base logits U_1 for a range of inputs produces a nontrivial next-token prediction (i.e., not always token 0) and matches the shape expected by downstream components.

verification.spec: Disable sequential head (zero its transition bias) and confidence head. Run inference on 32 diverse prompts. Collect argmax(U_1) across prompts and assert at least 8 distinct token IDs appear (i.e., predictions are input-dependent, not degenerate). Assert U shape (B, gamma, |V|).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the backbone forward is compatible with mini-batching, supporting anchor-bounded sequence packing where multiple independent draft anchors from the same document are packed into a single dense training batch via token-level attention indices (rather than 2D masks with padding).

verification.spec: Construct a packed batch with 3 independent anchors from separate documents packed into one sequence, with token-level attention indices. Run backbone forward and separately run backbone on each anchor individually. Assert per-anchor outputs match the packed run within 1e-4 (i.e., attention indices correctly isolate each anchor).

sub_tasks.requirements: The backbone's measured behavior matches the paper's reported first-position acceptance capacity for a parallel drafter, isolating the effect of the deep parallel backbone at position 1.

When running the DFlash-style parallel backbone (5 layers, block size 7) using Qwen3-4B as the target model and disabling the sequential head, the empirical position-1 conditional acceptance rate on the Math benchmark set is approximately 0.88 as reported in Figure 2.

verification.spec: Using Qwen3-4B as target with a 5-layer DFlash-style parallel backbone (block size 7, sequential head disabled), run speculative decoding on the Math benchmark set (GSM8K + MATH500 + AIME25). For each rollout, record acceptance at position 1 conditional on no prior rejections (trivially all instances). Report the average as position-1 conditional acceptance rate.

sub_tasks.requirements: When running the DFlash-style parallel backbone (5 layers, block size 7) using Qwen3-4B as the target model and disabling the sequential head, the empirical position-1 conditional acceptance rate on the Chat benchmark set is approximately 0.72 as reported in Figure 2.

verification.spec: Using Qwen3-4B as target with a 5-layer DFlash-style parallel backbone (block size 7, sequential head disabled), run speculative decoding on the Chat benchmark set (MT-Bench + Alpaca + Arena-Hard). Record acceptance at draft position 1 across all rollouts and report the average as position-1 conditional acceptance rate.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the lightweight sequential correction module in both Markov-head (low-rank W1 W2 transition bias, r=256) and RNN-head (gated recurrent update over state, previous-token embedding, and backbone hidden) forms, plugging transition biases into base logits via causal factorization.

Implement the causal factorization interface that combines parallel backbone base logits U_k with a prefix-dependent transition bias B_k to produce per-step conditional distributions p_k(x_k | x_0, x_<k) via a single softmax over U_k + B_k.

Code has been implemented that receives the parallel backbone outputs (hidden states h_1..h_gamma and base logits U_1..U_gamma over the vocabulary V) as inputs to the sequential stage, matching the interface described in Section 3.1's parallel stage.

verification.spec: Inspect the sequential head's forward signature (or call it) and assert it accepts backbone hidden states h (shape (B,gamma,d)) and base logits U (shape (B,gamma,|V|)) as inputs. Confirm both are used (non-trivially affect output) by ablating each to zero and checking output changes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the parallel backbone treats the anchor token itself as the first prediction position, feeding gamma input tokens (anchor + gamma-1 mask tokens) and producing gamma draft logits, per the modification described in Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Feed anchor token followed by (gamma-1) mask tokens into the backbone. Assert output logits tensor has gamma prediction positions (not gamma-1). Verify position 0's prediction corresponds to the token following the anchor (not the anchor itself).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes p_k(x_k | x_0, x_<k) as softmax(U_k + B_k(x_0, x_<k, .)) over the vocabulary V for each block position k, i.e., adds the transition bias to base logits before a single softmax normalization.

verification.spec: Instrument the sequential-stage sampling function. Feed known U_k and B_k tensors; assert the computed probability p_k equals softmax(U_k + B_k) via torch.allclose (i.e., bias is added to logits BEFORE a single softmax normalization, not applied post-softmax).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for sequential inference that samples draft tokens left-to-right within a block from p_k(. | x_0, x_<k), feeding each sampled token back into the sequential head to compute the bias for position k+1.

verification.spec: Instantiate the DSpark sequential head with a mock parallel backbone producing fixed base logits U_k. Run sequential inference for gamma=4 positions and verify: (1) at each step k the sampled token x_k is passed back into the head to compute the bias B_k(x_{k-1}) for position k+1; (2) monkey-patching the sampler to force x_1 to two different values yields different logits at position 2, confirming left-to-right causal conditioning; (3) the outputs match a reference implementation that manually loops p_k(.|x_0,x_<k).

sub_tasks.requirements: The sequential factorization yields exact per-token softmax probabilities (not globally normalized or marginalized over latent alignments), preserving compatibility with speculative decoding's rejection sampling rule as emphasized in the paper's discussion of CRF/CTC alternatives.

verification.spec: For a random draft distribution p_k(.|x_0,x_<k) produced by the sequential head, sum probabilities over the vocabulary and assert sum == 1 within 1e-5 (proper softmax). Assert no global partition function or latent-alignment marginalization exists in the code path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the Markov-head instantiation of the sequential block: low-rank factorization B = W1 W2 with W1 in R^{V x r}, W2 in R^{r x V}, and r=256 by default.

Code has been implemented that defines the Markov-head parameters W1 (shape V x r) and W2 (shape r x V) as learnable modules, where W1 functions as an embedding lookup table and W2 as a logit projection.

verification.spec: Import the Markov head module and assert it exposes two learnable parameters W1 and W2 (e.g., nn.Embedding of shape (V, r) or nn.Parameter of shape (V, r), and nn.Linear/Parameter of shape (r, V)). Verify parameter shapes match (V, r) and (r, V) with default r=256, that both require_grad=True, and that W1 is used as an embedding lookup (indexing by token id) while W2 projects r-dim vectors to V-dim logits.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Markov-head rank r is configurable and defaults to 256, matching the paper's default setting.

verification.spec: Load default config for the Markov head; assert config.markov_rank == 256 and instantiated W1.shape[1] == W2.shape[0] == 256. Confirm the rank is exposed as a config argument.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the Markov transition bias for position k as B(x_{k-1}, .) = W1[x_{k-1}] @ W2, using an embedding lookup on the previous token followed by projection to vocabulary size.

verification.spec: Access the Markov head module. Assert it has parameters W1 of shape (V, r) and W2 of shape (r, V). Call the module with a token id x_prev; verify the output equals W1[x_prev] @ W2 (shape (V,)) via torch.allclose against a manual computation.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Markov head depends only on the immediately preceding token x_{k-1} (first-order transition), with no state carried across positions beyond that token, as specified for the Markov-head variant.

verification.spec: Instantiate Markov head. Call it twice at position k with identical x_{k-1} but different x_{k-2},x_{k-3},...; assert outputs are bit-identical. Then vary x_{k-1} and confirm outputs differ.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that for position k=1 the Markov head uses the anchor token x_0 (the previous cycle's bonus token) as the conditioning predecessor, correctly bootstrapping the first block position.

verification.spec: Call the sequential head for position k=1, passing the anchor token id x_0. Assert the Markov transition bias used is W2[W1[x_0]] (verify by comparing to a manually computed W2 @ W1[x_0]).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Markov head is used as the default sequential-block variant in DSpark (both offline experiments and production DSpark-5), as stated in Sections 4.1, 4.3.2, and 5.1.

verification.spec: Load the default DSpark config file (and DSpark-5 production config). Assert sequential_head_type=='markov' in both.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the RNN-head instantiation of the sequential block: recurrent state s_k updated via a gated linear projection over the concatenation of previous state, previous-token embedding, and backbone hidden.

Code has been implemented that constructs the RNN-head input vector z_k = [s_{k-1}; W1[x_{k-1}]; h_k] as the concatenation of the recurrent state (size r), the previous-token embedding from W1 (size r), and the backbone hidden state (size d), yielding a vector of size 2r + d.

verification.spec: Instrument the RNN head's input-construction step. Pass known s_prev (shape (r,)), x_prev token id, and h_k (shape (d,)). Assert the constructed z_k tensor has shape (2r + d,) and equals torch.cat([s_prev, W1[x_prev], h_k], dim=-1) via torch.allclose.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that parameterizes W_g, W_c, W_o in R^{r x (2r + d)} via a single linear projection whose output is split into gate, candidate, and output components.

verification.spec: Import the RNN head module. Verify that it contains a single nn.Linear layer with in_features = 2*r + d and out_features = 3*r (fused gate/candidate/output), rather than three separate linear layers. Confirm the forward pass splits this projection's output into three r-dimensional chunks used as gate, candidate, and output components respectively.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that performs the gated recurrent update to produce s_k from z_k using W_g (gate), W_c (candidate), and W_o (output) with appropriate nonlinearities, following the equation given in Section 3.1's RNN-head description.

verification.spec: Instantiate the RNN head. Feed a known z_k tensor; hook internal computations to assert the module (1) computes gate g = sigmoid(W_g @ z_k), (2) computes candidate c = tanh(W_c @ z_k), (3) outputs s_k as an interpolation using g between prior state and candidate, and (4) applies W_o for the output projection. Verify via a manual numpy/torch replication that the module output matches the expected gated-recurrent formula.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code initializes the recurrent state s_0 to a zero vector of size r at the beginning of each draft block, per the paper's specification.

verification.spec: Instantiate the RNN sequential head. At the start of a new draft block, inspect the initial recurrent state and assert it is a zero tensor of shape (r,) (or (B, r)) matching the configured r.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that maps the recurrent state (or its output projection) to a vocabulary-sized transition bias B_k added to U_k to form the RNN-head conditional distribution at each position.

verification.spec: Run RNN head forward for a block and locate the projection producing B_k. Assert B_k has shape (|V|,). Assert final logits equal U_k + B_k (verify by hooking or by ablating W_o to zero and checking logits equal U_k).

sub_tasks.requirements: The RNN head shares the previous-token embedding table W1 with the Markov head (i.e., W1 is used for x_{k-1} lookup in both variants), consistent with the notation W1[x_{k-1}] in Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Instantiate both Markov and RNN heads within one DSpark model container. Assert the W1 parameter tensor used for x_{k-1} embedding lookup is the SAME object (id(W1_markov) == id(W1_rnn)) or has weight-tied storage.

sub_tasks.requirements: Ensure the sequential block satisfies the computational lightweight and behavioral properties required by the paper (T_sequential << T_parallel, mitigating multi-modal collision).

The sequential block is computationally lightweight relative to the parallel backbone so that overall draft latency remains dominated by the parallel stage (T_sequential << T_parallel), as required in Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Time one full DSpark draft forward on Qwen3-4B (batch=128, gamma=7) and separately time only the sequential head loop. Assert T_sequential / T_parallel < 0.1 (sequential overhead <10% of parallel backbone time).

sub_tasks.requirements: Given the illustrative two-mode context (e.g., 'of course' vs 'no problem'), a trained Markov head boosts the logit of 'course' and suppresses 'problem' at position 2 after 'of' is sampled at position 1, demonstrating mitigation of cross-mode collision as described.

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic bimodal training set with two contexts leading to 'of course' vs 'no problem'. Train the Markov head to convergence. At inference, condition on 'of' at position 1 and inspect position-2 logits; assert logit('course') > logit('problem') by at least 1.0. Repeat with 'no' and assert logit('problem') > logit('course').

sub_tasks.requirements: The sequential loop iterates strictly left-to-right (position 1 through gamma) and each position's sampled token feeds forward into subsequent position(s), so the intra-block causal factorization is respected during draft generation.

verification.spec: Hook the sequential head's sampling loop to log the order of positions computed. Assert positions are visited in order 1,2,...,gamma. Then intercept the sampled token at position k and modify it; assert the position k+1 logit changes accordingly (confirming forward feed of sampled tokens).

sub_tasks.requirements: The sequential head selection between Markov and RNN variants is exposed as a configuration option in the training/inference codepath so both variants can be trained and evaluated under identical protocols (used for the Section 4.3.2 comparison).

verification.spec: Load the training config schema and assert a field like 'sequential_head_type' (or equivalent) accepts values 'markov' and 'rnn'. Instantiate DSpark twice with each value and assert the sequential head module class differs accordingly.

sub_tasks.requirements: Validate the sequential-head design choices numerically against paper claims.

On the proposal-length sweep with Qwen3-4B (Figure 4, left three panels), the RNN-head variant yields only marginal additional accepted-length improvements over the Markov-head variant, primarily at longer proposal lengths, matching the paper's claim justifying Markov as the default.

verification.spec: Train DSpark-Markov and DSpark-RNN on Qwen3-4B with identical config, evaluate accepted length on GSM8K/MATH500/AIME25/MBPP/HumanEval/LCB/MT-Bench/Alpaca/Arena-Hard at gamma in {4,8,12,16}. Compute average (RNN - Markov) across benchmarks per gamma; assert improvement is <=0.15 tokens at each gamma and larger at gamma=15 than at gamma=3.

sub_tasks.requirements: The added per-round latency from the Markov sequential loop over the DFlash baseline is small (approximately 0.2%-1.3% when scaling draft length from 4 to 16 at batch size 128, averaged over context lengths {512,1024,2048,4096}), as reported in the rightmost panel of Figure 4.

verification.spec: Using Qwen3-4B with a 5-layer DSpark (Markov head) and DFlash baseline, measure per-round engine latency at batch size 128 averaged over context lengths {512,1024,2048,4096} for draft lengths {4,8,12,16}. Compute the percent latency overhead of DSpark over DFlash at each draft length and verify it falls in ~0.2%-1.3%.

sub_tasks.requirements: With the Markov head enabled, the DSpark draft model attains high position-1 conditional acceptance on Qwen3-4B math (approximately 0.93 as reported in Figure 2), inheriting the parallel backbone's initial-token accuracy.

verification.spec: Run speculative decoding rollouts of DSpark (Markov head) with Qwen3-4B target on math benchmarks (GSM8K/MATH500/AIME25). Compute position-wise conditional acceptance rate at draft position 1 (fraction accepted at pos 1 among all draft blocks). Verify value is approximately 0.93.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the per-position confidence head predicting conditional prefix survival probability, its supervision via analytical acceptance rate from total variation distance, and post-hoc Sequential Temperature Scaling (STS) calibration minimizing ECE over cumulative products.
The confidence head module architecture predicts a scalar conditional survival probability per draft position.
Code has been implemented defining a confidence head module consisting of a lightweight linear projection followed by a sigmoid activation, producing an output c_k in (0,1) per draft position.

verification.spec: Import the confidence head module and inspect its architecture: verify it consists of a single nn.Linear projection followed by a sigmoid activation (torch.sigmoid or nn.Sigmoid), producing scalar per-position outputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the confidence head input at position k concatenates the backbone hidden state h_k with the Markov embedding W1[x_{k-1}] of the previously sampled/anchor token.

verification.spec: Instantiate the confidence head with known input dimensions. Trace the forward pass and verify the input at position k is the concatenation of backbone hidden state h_k (dim d) and Markov embedding W1[x_{k-1}] (dim r), yielding an input of dim d+r.

sub_tasks.requirements: The confidence head shares/reuses the Markov head's W1 embedding table for the previous-token feature (rather than instantiating a fresh embedding), keeping the head lightweight.

verification.spec: Verify by object identity (id() or is) that the W1 parameter tensor used by the confidence head to embed the previous token is the same Parameter as the Markov head's W1 embedding table (shared reference), not a separate copy.

sub_tasks.requirements: Confidence head forward returns a per-position tensor of shape (batch, gamma) with values strictly in (0,1) suitable for interpretation as conditional acceptance probabilities.

verification.spec: Call the confidence head forward on a random batch (B, gamma) of hidden states and prev-token IDs. Assert output shape == (B, gamma) and all values strictly in (0, 1) via 0 < out < 1 element-wise.

sub_tasks.requirements: Supervision of confidence head via analytical soft acceptance targets derived from total variation distance.
Code has been implemented that computes the per-step analytical acceptance target c*_k = 1 - 0.5 * ||p_k^d - p_k^t||_1 between draft and target distributions at each draft position.

verification.spec: Construct hand-crafted draft and target categorical distributions p_d, p_t. Call the implementation's soft-label function and verify the output equals 1 - 0.5*sum(|p_d - p_t|) to within 1e-6 for multiple random cases.

sub_tasks.requirements: The soft label c*_k is computed using the frozen target model's probability distribution (obtained via the shared LM head applied to target hidden states) and is treated as a detached (non-differentiable) target for the confidence loss.

verification.spec: Run one training step and confirm (1) target model parameters have requires_grad=False, (2) the tensor holding c*_k has requires_grad=False or is produced under torch.no_grad(), and (3) the target distribution is derived by applying the shared frozen LM head to target hidden states.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the confidence loss L_conf as a per-position binary cross-entropy between predicted c_k and analytical target c*_k, position-weighted by w_k = exp(-(k-1)/gamma), averaged over positions and samples.

verification.spec: Given a batch of predicted c_k and soft-label c*_k, compute reference L_conf = mean over samples of sum_k w_k * BCE(c_k, c*_k) with w_k = exp(-(k-1)/gamma). Compare to the implementation's L_conf output; assert equality within 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Verify numerically that L_conf reduces to zero when the predicted c_k exactly matches c*_k for a hand-constructed input, ensuring correctness of the BCE-with-soft-labels implementation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Sequential Temperature Scaling (STS) post-hoc calibration procedure over cumulative prefix products.

Code has been implemented that, given a held-out validation set of draft rollouts, records per-position predicted confidences c_1..c_gamma and empirical binary acceptance indicators for each draft position (with prior positions accepted).

verification.spec: Run the calibration data collection pipeline on a held-out validation set of speculative rollouts. Verify the resulting artifact contains, per rollout and per position k in 1..gamma, both the predicted confidence c_k and a binary indicator of whether the token at position k was accepted by the target given prior positions were accepted.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented computing the cumulative prefix survival probability a_k = prod_{i<=k} c_i for each position, and the empirical prefix-acceptance indicator (all positions 1..k accepted) as the calibration target.

verification.spec: For a batch of collected per-position c_k arrays, verify the implementation computes a_k = cumulative product prod_{i<=k} c_i (compare to numpy.cumprod). Verify the empirical prefix-acceptance indicator equals AND of per-position accept flags for i=1..k.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) function that bins predicted probabilities and computes the weighted average of |accuracy(bin) - confidence(bin)| following Naeini et al. (2015).

verification.spec: Call the ECE function on a synthetic dataset (e.g., predictions uniform in [0,1] with known miscalibration). Compare with a reference implementation of Naeini et al. (2015) equal-width binning ECE, using the same bin count; assert equality within 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: STS calibration runs sequentially k=1..gamma: at each position it performs a 1D grid search over a temperature scalar T_k to minimize ECE of the cumulative product a_k, while keeping temperatures for positions <k fixed at their previously chosen values.

verification.spec: Run STS on a validation set with gamma=5. Verify (1) fitting proceeds in order k=1,2,...,gamma; (2) at each k, only T_k is optimized via 1D grid search minimizing ECE of cumulative product a_k; (3) after fitting T_k, subsequent iterations do not modify T_{<k} (check T_j values before and after fitting T_{j+1}).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that temperature scaling is applied to the pre-sigmoid logit (or equivalent sigmoid-with-temperature parameterization) of the confidence head output, ensuring the transformation is monotonic and thus order-preserving over draft tokens.

verification.spec: Inspect the STS transform: verify it applies T to the pre-sigmoid logit z as sigmoid(z/T) (or equivalent form). Numerically verify monotonicity: for a strictly increasing sequence of raw logits, the STS-transformed sigmoid outputs are also strictly increasing for any T>0.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit-test-style check verifies that applying STS with the fitted per-position temperatures preserves the ranking of draft tokens (identical argsort of c_k across a validation batch before vs. after scaling at each position).

verification.spec: For a validation batch, compute argsort of raw c_k across tokens at each position k. Apply STS with fitted T_k. Recompute argsort of scaled outputs. Assert element-wise equality of the two argsort arrays for every position.

sub_tasks.requirements: The fitted STS temperatures {T_1,...,T_gamma} are persisted (e.g., saved to disk with the drafter checkpoint) and are loaded at inference time to transform raw confidence outputs before being consumed by the hardware-aware scheduler.

verification.spec: Run STS fitting, verify it writes T_1..T_gamma to disk (e.g., a .pt/.json file bundled with the drafter checkpoint). Restart process, load the checkpoint, and verify the inference-time confidence pipeline reads these temperatures and applies them before scheduler input (e.g., by mocking scheduler input and checking scaled vs. raw values).

verification.spec: On Alpaca rollouts with Qwen3-4B DSpark, compute ROC-AUC of predicted cumulative acceptance a_k against binary prefix-acceptance labels at positions {1,3,5,7}. Verify each falls within approximately [0.81, 0.90].

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the greedy hardware-aware prefix scheduler (Algorithm 1) that maximizes expected throughput Θ = τ · SPS(B) using cumulative survival probabilities, engine-profiled SPS lookup table, and early-stopping to preserve the non-anticipating property.
Cumulative prefix survival probability computation.

Code has been implemented to accept, for each active request r in {1,...,R}, a per-position confidence sequence c_{r,1},...,c_{r,γ} produced by the (calibrated) confidence head and to expose it as the scheduler input.

verification.spec: Invoke the scheduler entrypoint with a mock batch of R>=2 requests each carrying a c_{r,1..gamma} tensor. Verify the scheduler accepts this input without error and internally accesses these per-request confidence sequences (e.g., asserts shape (R, gamma) and dtype float).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute prefix survival probabilities a_{r,j} = Π_{i≤j} c_{r,i} for j = 1,...,γ for every active request (Algorithm 1 lines 1–3).

verification.spec: Feed the scheduler a known c_{r,1..gamma} matrix. Extract the computed a_{r,j}. Assert element-wise equality with numpy.cumprod(c, axis=1) within 1e-6 for multiple random inputs.
