sub_tasks.requirements: Engine-profiled SPS(B) capacity lookup table.

Code has been implemented to profile, once at engine initialization, the engine's steps-per-second SPS(B) as a function of forward-pass batch size B (in tokens) and to persist the resulting curve as a lightweight cost table.

verification.spec: Invoke engine initialization and verify (1) an SPS(B) profiling routine is executed once, sweeping forward-pass batch sizes over a defined range, timing steps to compute steps/sec, and (2) the resulting curve is persisted as a lookup table (dict/tensor/file) accessible to the scheduler at runtime.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that exposes an O(1) SPS(B) lookup used by the scheduler at every admission step, rather than recomputing engine throughput on the fly.

verification.spec: Inspect scheduler module: confirm there is an SPS lookup object (e.g., dict, tensor, or callable with O(1) indexing) that is precomputed at engine init and queried inside the admission loop. Verify by patching the SPS lookup with a MagicMock and asserting it is called (not recomputed) once per admission step.

sub_tasks.requirements: The profiled SPS(B) table covers the full range of batch sizes B that can be produced by admitting up to γ tokens per request across R concurrent requests (B ∈ [R, R·(1+γ)]).

verification.spec: Build the SPS profile for a test engine configuration with R concurrent requests and block size gamma. Assert that SPS(B) is defined (non-None, finite) for every integer B in [R, R*(1+gamma)].

sub_tasks.requirements: Candidate extension pool construction and global sorting.
Code has been implemented to build the candidate space E = {(r, j) | a_{r,j} > 0} spanning all requests and all draft positions j ∈ {1,...,γ}.

verification.spec: Call the scheduler with synthetic confidence tensors of shape (R, gamma) containing a mix of zero and positive per-position survival values. Inspect the constructed candidate set E and assert it equals {(r,j): a_{r,j} > 0} across all r in [0,R), j in [1,gamma].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to sort E in descending order of a_{r,j} (Algorithm 1 line 4) prior to greedy admission.

verification.spec: Instrument the scheduler to expose the sorted candidate iteration order. Feed synthetic a_{r,j} values with known ordering; assert the iteration visits candidates in monotonically non-increasing a_{r,j} order.

sub_tasks.requirements: Because a_{r,j} is monotonically non-increasing in j, iterating E in descending order of a_{r,j} respects intra-request prefix order: for any request r, (r, j) is admitted only after (r, j-1) has already been admitted.

verification.spec: Generate random confidence tensors, run the scheduler, and record admission order. For every request r and every admitted position j > 1, assert (r, j-1) was admitted at an earlier step in the sorted iteration.

sub_tasks.requirements: Greedy admission loop with throughput tracking.

Code has been implemented to initialize per-request selected lengths ℓ_r = 0, batch size B = R, expected accepted tokens τ* = R, and best throughput Θ_best = R · SPS(R) prior to admission (Algorithm 1 lines 5–6).

verification.spec: Invoke the scheduler on a mocked SPS callback that records its call sequence. Assert the first computed Theta_best equals R * SPS(R), initial B == R, initial tau* == R, and initial per-request lengths are all 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: On admitting (r, j) from the sorted pool, the scheduler updates ℓ_r ← j, increments B ← B + 1, and accumulates τ* ← τ* + a_{r,j} (Algorithm 1 line 8).

verification.spec: Run scheduler on a small deterministic input and trace admission-loop state. Assert that after admitting each (r,j) the tracked B increments by exactly 1 and tau* increments by exactly a_{r,j}, and ell_r updates to j.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to evaluate the current expected throughput Θ = τ* · SPS(B) after every admission using the profiled cost table (Algorithm 1 line 9).

verification.spec: Mock SPS(B) with a known function and run the scheduler. Assert that after each admission the tracked Theta equals tau* * SPS(B) computed with the mocked callable (bit-exact within float tolerance).

sub_tasks.requirements: Whenever Θ > Θ_best the scheduler updates Θ_best ← Θ and commits the current lengths to the returned selection ℓ*_r ← ℓ_r for all r (Algorithm 1 lines 10–11).

verification.spec: Craft an input where Theta strictly increases at every admission for the first k steps. Assert that after the loop Theta_best equals the last Theta value and returned ell*_r matches the ell_r state at that admission.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler ultimately returns the tuple (ℓ*_1,...,ℓ*_R) corresponding to the highest observed Θ_best, with each ℓ*_r ∈ {0,...,γ}.

verification.spec: Call the scheduler and assert the return is a tuple/list of length R, each element an int in [0, gamma], and that reconstructing Theta = (R + sum_r ell*_r + R*...) yields Theta_best.

sub_tasks.requirements: Early-stopping and non-anticipating property enforcement.

Code has been implemented to break out of the admission loop immediately when the newly computed Θ is not strictly greater than Θ_best (Algorithm 1 lines 12–14), rather than continuing a retrospective global search.

verification.spec: Construct a scenario where Theta strictly increases for 3 steps then decreases. Assert the scheduler exits after the first drop (does not visit the remaining candidates), verified by tracing the number of SPS calls == 4.

sub_tasks.requirements: As a consequence of early-stopping, for every request r the returned ℓ*_r depends only on confidence values c_{r,1},...,c_{r,ℓ*_r} and never on c_{r,ℓ*_r+1} or later positions, preserving the non-anticipating property required for lossless speculative decoding.

verification.spec: For a batch of R=2 requests, run the scheduler once; then perturb c_{r, ell*_r + 1} (and later positions) arbitrarily while keeping earlier positions fixed, and rerun. Assert ell*_r is identical across both runs for every r.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test reproduces the Appendix A counterexample: on a two-token vocabulary with p_t(A)=0.7, p_t(B)=0.3, p_d(A)=p_d(B)=0.5, and a retrospective scheduler that sets ℓ=2 iff x_1=A, the induced first-output distribution is (0.85, 0.15) — deviating from the target (0.7, 0.3) — while the causal Algorithm-1 scheduler with early-stopping instead returns ℓ=0 for that request (because Θ_1 < Θ_0), recovering the exact target distribution.

verification.spec: Implement the Appendix A toy setup (vocab {A,B}, p_t=(0.7,0.3), p_d=(0.5,0.5), a_1=0.8). Simulate 10^6 rounds with (i) a retrospective scheduler that sets ell=2 iff x_1=A and ell=0 otherwise, and (ii) the causal Algorithm-1 scheduler. Assert retrospective empirical P(x=A) is within 0.01 of 0.85, and causal empirical P(x=A) is within 0.01 of 0.7.

sub_tasks.requirements: Integration with confidence head and target verification pipeline.

Code has been implemented to consume calibrated (post-STS) confidence scores as c_{r,i} inputs, so that a_{r,j} corresponds to a properly calibrated cumulative acceptance probability rather than raw overconfident scores.

verification.spec: Inspect the code path that feeds confidence scores to the scheduler: confirm calibrated (post-STS) scores are used (e.g., scores pass through an STS.apply() or equivalent temperature-scaling module) rather than the raw sigmoid outputs of the confidence head.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to route, for each request r, only the prefix of the drafted block of length ℓ*_r into the target model's verification pass, dropping draft tokens at positions j > ℓ*_r before verification.

verification.spec: Mock the target verification kernel to record the shape/lengths of received prefixes per request. Run one decoding cycle with scheduler outputs (ell*_1,...,ell*_R). Assert request r contributes exactly ell*_r draft tokens to the verification batch and that tokens at positions j>ell*_r are absent.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler is invoked once per decoding cycle across the current batch of active requests and returns per-request verification lengths that are then fed to the target-model verification kernel.

verification.spec: Run 5 decoding cycles in a mock serving loop with 3 active requests. Assert scheduler.__call__ is invoked exactly once per cycle, receives the current batch's confidence tensor of shape (R, gamma), and its returned lengths tuple is what parameterizes the verification kernel call.

sub_tasks.requirements: Correctness and consistency of the scheduler as a component.

A unit test verifies that when SPS(B) is set to a constant, the scheduler admits all candidates (r, j) with a_{r,j} > 0 in decreasing order and returns ℓ*_r = γ for every request (since Θ = τ*·SPS grows monotonically).

verification.spec: Set SPS(B) := 1.0 for all B. Feed random positive confidences c_{r,j} in (0,1) for R=3, gamma=5. Assert the scheduler returns ell*_r = gamma = 5 for every request.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that when the profiled SPS(B) decays fast enough that R · SPS(R) already exceeds (R + a_{r,j}) · SPS(R+1) for all first candidates, the scheduler halts immediately and returns ℓ*_r = 0 for all r.

verification.spec: Choose SPS(B) with very steep decay (e.g., SPS(B) = 1/B^10) so that R*SPS(R) > (R+a_max)*SPS(R+1) for the max a_{r,j}<1. Run the scheduler and assert returned ell*_r = 0 for all r and Theta_best == R*SPS(R).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that on a two-request example with distinct confidence profiles the scheduler allocates a longer verification length to the request with globally higher a_{r,j} values, matching a hand-computed Θ trajectory.

verification.spec: Set R=2 with c_1 = [0.95,0.9,0.8,0.7,0.6] and c_2 = [0.5,0.3,0.1,0.05,0.02], and a mildly decreasing SPS. Hand-compute the Theta trajectory step by step, then assert scheduler returns lengths matching the hand-computed argmax (ell*_1 > ell*_2).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that with lossless-only downstream verification enabled, running end-to-end speculative decoding with the causal Algorithm-1 scheduler produces output token distributions statistically indistinguishable from target-only sampling, whereas a retrospective (no early-stop) variant is empirically detectable as biased.

verification.spec: Using a small mock target/draft pair with known distributions, simulate 5e5 decoding steps under (a) Algorithm-1 causal scheduler + lossless verification and (b) retrospective (no early-stop) scheduler + lossless verification. Assert the empirical first-token distribution of (a) matches target sampling within TV distance 0.01, while (b) deviates by > 0.03.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the composite training objective (weighted cross-entropy, total-variation, confidence BCE) with position weights and default coefficients, sample multiple anchor positions per sequence, freeze target model and shared embedding/LM head, and train the drafter for 10 epochs.
Implement the composite loss L = alpha_ce * L_ce + alpha_tv * L_tv + alpha_conf * L_conf with position-weighted terms.
Implement the position weighting schedule w_k = exp(-(k-1)/gamma), applied identically to all three loss terms across positions k = 1..gamma.
Code has been implemented that computes per-position weights w_k = exp(-(k-1)/gamma) as a tensor of length gamma and exposes it for reuse across all three loss terms.

verification.spec: Import the weight-computation function/module and evaluate at gamma=7. Assert output is a tensor of shape (7,) equal (within 1e-6) to [exp(-(k-1)/7) for k=1..7]. Verify it is exposed to all three loss modules via a shared attribute or argument.

sub_tasks.requirements: The position-weight tensor satisfies w_1 = 1.0 and w_gamma = exp(-(gamma-1)/gamma) at the configured block size, verifiable by direct evaluation.

verification.spec: For the configured block size gamma (read from config), compute the position-weight tensor and assert w[0] == 1.0 (within 1e-6) and w[-1] == exp(-(gamma-1)/gamma) (within 1e-6).

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the cross-entropy loss L_ce that trains the drafter to predict the ground-truth token at each block position, weighted by w_k.
Code has been implemented that computes L_ce = -sum_k w_k * log p_k^d(x_k*) using the drafter's causal block distribution p_k^d incorporating the sequential head's transition bias.

verification.spec: Build a mock drafter producing per-position causal distributions p_k^d (via the sequential head) and ground-truth tokens x_k*. Compute L_ce via the implementation and independently via -sum_k w_k*log p_k^d(x_k*) in numpy; assert equality within 1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: L_ce is normalized consistently across a batch (e.g., averaged over anchor blocks) and produces finite, differentiable gradients that flow into the backbone and sequential head parameters.

verification.spec: Run L_ce on a batch of 8 sequences, assert the returned scalar is finite and matches the documented normalization (average over anchor blocks). Call .backward() and assert gradients on backbone and sequential head parameters are non-zero and finite.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the total-variation distribution-matching loss L_tv between draft p_k^d and (stop-gradient) target p_k^t, weighted by w_k.
Code has been implemented that computes L_tv = sum_k w_k * (1/2) * ||p_k^d - p_k^t||_1 with the target distribution detached from the computation graph.

verification.spec: Compute L_tv on mock p_k^d (with grad) and p_k^t (detached). Independently compute sum_k w_k * 0.5 * ||p_k^d - p_k^t||_1 in numpy; assert equality within 1e-5. Additionally assert p_k^t.requires_grad is False and no gradient flows through the target branch by inspecting p_k^t.grad_fn is None.

sub_tasks.requirements: L_tv evaluates to 0 (within numerical tolerance) when the draft distribution equals the target distribution and is upper-bounded by w_k summed for any distributions.

verification.spec: Construct two identical categorical distributions p_d = p_t (e.g., softmax over random logits) and verify that L_tv computed by the implementation returns 0 (abs value < 1e-5). Then construct arbitrary distributions and verify L_tv <= sum_k w_k (since TV distance is bounded by 1 per position).

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the confidence BCE loss L_conf that supervises c_k against the analytical soft acceptance label c_k* = 1 - (1/2)||p_k^d - p_k^t||_1, weighted by w_k.
Code has been implemented that computes the soft label c_k* per position from the (detached) draft and target distributions using the total variation formulation.

verification.spec: Import the function computing c_k*; feed known draft and target distributions and verify the output equals 1 - 0.5 * ||p_d - p_t||_1 elementwise per position. Also verify that gradients from c_k* do not flow back into p_d or p_t (detached inputs).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes L_conf = -sum_k w_k * [c_k* log c_k + (1 - c_k*) log(1 - c_k)] with numerically stable BCE (e.g., log-sigmoid formulation) and gradients flowing only to the confidence head.

verification.spec: Compute L_conf on synthetic (c_k*, c_k logits) inputs using the implementation and compare against a reference BCE-with-logits computation (position-weighted by w_k = exp(-(k-1)/gamma)); assert max abs diff < 1e-5. Check numerical stability at extreme logits (e.g., +/-50). Verify gradients on backbone/sequential-head parameters coming from L_conf are zero (only confidence-head params get gradient).

sub_tasks.requirements: The composite loss uses default coefficients alpha_ce = 0.1, alpha_tv = 0.9, alpha_conf = 1.0, exposed as configurable hyperparameters with these defaults.

verification.spec: Inspect the training config/dataclass and confirm defaults alpha_ce=0.1, alpha_tv=0.9, alpha_conf=1.0 are set; verify these are user-overridable via CLI/config and that the total loss is computed as alpha_ce*L_ce + alpha_tv*L_tv + alpha_conf*L_conf.

sub_tasks.requirements: Sample multiple anchor positions per target sequence and construct gamma-token training blocks from them.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the Markov head transition bias as a low-rank factorization B = W1 W2 (W1 in R^{V x r}, W2 in R^{r x V}) with default r=256, such that B_k = W2^T W1[x_{k-1}] when queried with previous token x_{k-1}.

verification.spec: Instantiate MarkovHead(V=1024, r=256); assert W1.shape==(1024,256) and W2.shape==(256,1024); call with x_{k-1}=tensor of ids and assert output shape == (batch, V) and matches W1[x_{k-1}] @ W2 numerically.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the RNN head gated update with input z_k = [s_{k-1}; W1[x_{k-1}]; h_k] in R^{2r+d}, using a single linear projection W in R^{r x (2r+d)} split into gate, candidate, and output components, with s_0 initialized to zero.

verification.spec: Instantiate RNNHead(r=256, d=512); assert the fused projection weight has shape (3*r, 2*r+d); run one step with s_0=0 and assert output state has shape (batch, r) and differs from s_0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the confidence head as c_k = sigmoid(w^T [h_k ; W1[x_{k-1}]]) producing a scalar in (0,1) per draft position.

verification.spec: Instantiate ConfidenceHead; feed random h_k and x_{k-1}; assert output shape == (batch, gamma), all values in (0,1), and that changing x_{k-1} changes c_k.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the analytical per-step acceptance target c*_k = 1 - 0.5 * ||p^d_k - p^t_k||_1 (or equivalent formulation of acceptance in terms of total variation distance).

verification.spec: Compute c*_k for two known distributions p_d and p_t; assert |c*_k - (1 - 0.5*sum(|p_d - p_t|))| < 1e-6; assert c*_k == 1.0 when p_d == p_t and c*_k == 0.0 when supports are disjoint.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the position-weighted cross-entropy loss L_ce = sum_k w_k * CE(p^d_k, x*_k) with weights w_k = exp(-(k-1)/gamma).

verification.spec: Given fixed logits and labels, compute L_ce with the implementation and compare against a manual reference computing sum_k exp(-(k-1)/gamma) * F.cross_entropy(logits_k, labels_k); assert equality within 1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the position-weighted total-variation distribution matching loss L_tv = sum_k w_k * 0.5 * ||p^d_k - p^t_k||_1 with w_k = exp(-(k-1)/gamma).

verification.spec: Given draft and target distributions, compute L_tv and assert it equals sum_k w_k * 0.5 * torch.sum(torch.abs(p_d_k - p_t_k)) within 1e-5; assert L_tv == 0 when p_d == p_t.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the position-weighted binary cross-entropy confidence loss L_conf = sum_k w_k * BCE(c_k, c*_k) with w_k = exp(-(k-1)/gamma) and c*_k the analytical soft acceptance label.

verification.spec: Given fixed c_k and c*_k tensors, compute L_conf and compare to sum_k w_k * F.binary_cross_entropy(c_k, c*_k) within 1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the confidence head consists of a linear projection applied to the concatenation of the backbone hidden state h_k and the Markov embedding W1[x_{k-1}] followed by a sigmoid, producing a scalar c_k in (0,1) per draft position.

verification.spec: Instantiate the confidence head; pass a random hidden state h_k of shape (B, d) and a previous-token index tensor; verify output shape is (B,) or (B,1), every value lies strictly in (0,1), and that the module contains exactly one linear layer with input dim d + r followed by a sigmoid activation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the analytical acceptance-rate supervision target computes c*_k = 1 - 0.5 * ||p^d_k - p^t_k||_1 per Equation 8.

verification.spec: Construct several pairs of draft/target distributions (identical, disjoint, and partially overlapping); apply the supervision function and assert results equal 1.0, 0.0, and 1 - 0.5*L1_distance respectively within 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Sequential Temperature Scaling (STS) performs a left-to-right 1D grid search over per-position temperatures on a held-out validation set, at each position k choosing the temperature that minimizes the Expected Calibration Error of the cumulative product prod_{i<=k} c_i while keeping temperatures at positions <k fixed.

verification.spec: Generate synthetic overconfident sigmoid outputs and empirical acceptance labels; run STS across gamma=5 positions; assert (1) temperatures are optimized position-by-position sequentially, (2) each position's ECE of the cumulative product after calibration is <= ECE before calibration, and (3) relative ordering of raw scores within a position is preserved.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the hardware-aware prefix scheduler follows Algorithm 1: it constructs prefix survival probabilities a_{r,j} = prod_{i<=j} c_{r,i}, sorts all (r,j) candidates descending by a_{r,j}, greedily admits them updating B, tau*, and Theta = tau* * SPS(B), and breaks immediately when Theta does not improve, returning per-request lengths achieving Theta_best.

verification.spec: Construct R=3 requests with hand-crafted confidence sequences and a monotonically decreasing SPS(B) lookup; run scheduler; verify (1) candidates are processed in globally sorted order of a_{r,j}, (2) early-stopping triggers as soon as Theta decreases, (3) returned lengths achieve the recorded Theta_best, and (4) a scripted counterexample where confidences would otherwise be leaked halts before evaluating the leaking position.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the production asynchronous scheduler estimates upcoming verification capacity K using confidence outputs from two steps prior, removes the early-stopping break to perform an unconstrained global search bounded by K, and still sorts current-step candidates by up-to-date cumulative confidence — implementing dynamic top-K admission compatible with Zero-Overhead Scheduling.

verification.spec: Simulate a two-step pipeline: feed confidence outputs c^{(t-2)} to determine K, then feed different c^{(t)} to determine ordering; assert (1) K depends only on c^{(t-2)}, not c^{(t)}, (2) top-K selection uses c^{(t)} rankings, and (3) with a jagged SPS curve the async scheduler admits more tokens than the synchronous early-stopping variant.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the engine profiles the SPS(B) capacity curve once during engine initialization and stores it as a lightweight cost table that the scheduler looks up rather than recomputing.

verification.spec: Import engine module; instantiate engine; assert an SPS cost table (dict or tensor) is populated during initialization keyed by batch size B, and that the scheduler performs O(1) lookups (no forward passes) when computing Theta.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that all three training losses (L_ce, L_tv, L_conf) apply position weighting w_k = exp(-(k-1)/gamma) that emphasizes earlier block positions.

verification.spec: Set gamma=7 and compute weights for k=1..7; assert w_1 = 1.0 and w_k = exp(-(k-1)/7) within 1e-6; verify each of L_ce, L_tv, L_conf incorporates these weights by comparing losses computed with uniform vs exponential weighting on synthetic inputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the cross-entropy loss L_ce is the position-weighted negative log-likelihood of the ground-truth token x*_k under the draft distribution p^d_k as defined in Section 3.3.

verification.spec: On synthetic draft logits of shape (B, gamma, V) and ground-truth token ids, assert L_ce equals the position-weighted average of -log p^d_k(x*_k) within 1e-5; verify gradient flows into the draft logits only.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the distribution-matching loss L_tv computes the position-weighted total variation distance 0.5 * ||p^d_k - p^t_k||_1 between draft and target distributions.

verification.spec: For identical draft/target distributions, assert L_tv = 0; for disjoint one-hot distributions, assert L_tv = 1 (before weighting); for random distributions, assert L_tv equals the reference position-weighted 0.5*L1 within 1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that L_conf is a position-weighted binary cross-entropy loss between the predicted confidence c_k and the soft acceptance label c*_k from Equation 8.

verification.spec: Feed synthetic c_k values and matching c*_k soft targets; assert L_conf equals reference position-weighted BCE(c_k, c*_k) within 1e-5; verify loss is minimized (approaches 0) when c_k = c*_k.

verification.spec: Import the training loss combination function/module; verify that the default coefficients for the cross-entropy, total-variation, and confidence losses are 0.1, 0.9, and 1.0 respectively (e.g., inspect config defaults or call the loss function with known component inputs and assert total == 0.1*L_ce + 0.9*L_tv + 1.0*L_conf within a small numerical tolerance)
